changes.change: Steele starts in goal, Kinsky benched
changes.note: A deliberate punt, not a risk. Per FPL auto-sub rules, if Steele does not play, Kinsky comes in by default - the floor is covered either way. The upside: Steele's rare starts have been strong, and Coventry away (difficulty 2) is the softest fixture on the squad. Standing rule in the model: a non-starting keeper in the XI is a free swing when the backup's minutes are secure - only keeper risk that gets flagged from now on is doubt over the BACKUP's minutes.

A fixture play: Ipswich at home (difficulty 2) instead of away to Man City (difficulty 4). The engine is split - Mitchell fails consistency (0.333) and the team-proof screen; Guehi clears both (3.33 ppm, 0.667) but faces the hardest fixture on the slate. Acceptable for one week; reverse it once the fixture turns unless Mitchell's side stabilises.

Calvert-Lewin's dials are weak across the board (1.67 ppm, 0.333 consistency). Tzolis reads a perfect 1.000 consistency, but on 210 minutes - a thin sample. Fixtures are roughly level (Sunderland away 3 vs Newcastle home 2). Lean yes, with eyes open: this is a minutes bet, not a proven edge.

Clean swap. Isak at home to Fulham (difficulty 2), 0.667 consistency, versus Bruno at home to Man City (difficulty 4) on 0.333 consistency with his season propped by one 23-point haul. This is exactly the captaincy logic the backtest supports.

squad_strategy.gk_punt_rule: A deliberately non-starting GK in the XI is an intended auto-sub play, never a news flag. Floor = backup's minutes; upside = the punt keeper's favourable fixture. Flag keeper risk only when the BACKUP's minutes are in doubt.
